messages:
OncallBot: :rotating_light: Pager: incidents - elevated control-plane 5xx rate detected (5xx spike -> auth/org-lookup/config/billing). alert_id=cp-5xx-stack-2177777777
Alex K: seeing it too, dashboard lit up. which dependency is the source?
Samir: quick summary from metrics: control-plane 5xx rate jump at 17:45 UTC, sustained. traces show majority originate from `org-lookup` and `config-service` timeouts. auth also shows higher latencies and token validation retries.
Jordan: logs -> repeated `504 gateway timeout` from config-service to billing-client. snippet: ```ERROR config-client - upstream billing-service 504 after 10s```.
Maria: any recent deploys? I see a config push at ~17:40 UTC that touched rollout flags for org-lookup caching TTLs.
Alex K: yeah config push 17:39 by infra-bot. probable correlation.
Samir: starting mitigation steps: 1) scale config-service, 2) rollback TTL change if scaling doesn't help, 3) enable short-circuit org-lookup cache bypass for known healthy orgs.
Lia: paging CS/Support: flagging that some customers report API 500s on model inference. CS ticket queue rising. Lia -> I'll add severity note and list top 5 customers impacted.
Jordan: performing `kubectl scale deployment config-service --replicas=6 -n controlplane` now.
OpsBot: command executed: replicas for config-service scaled from 2 to 6.
Samir: added temporary circuit breaker on billing-client (fail fast after 3s) to avoid head-of-line blocking.
Maria: running a quick rollback of the TTL change: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/config-service --to-revision=3` - starting.
OncallBot: Deploy bot: rollback initiated by Maria at 17:52 UTC.
Alex K: while rollback is in progress, enable token caching in the auth proxy to cut org lookup calls: patching auth-proxy config.
Samir: patch applied: `AUTH_PROXY_CACHE_TTL=60s` for token validation; deployed to canary.
Jordan: seeing 5xx drop in control-plane from 18% -> 6% in the last 3m. latency still elevated but trending down.
Lia: rough customer impact: approx 9% of API requests failed over the spike window, about 14 customers saw >1% error rates, two customers had sustained errors (acct-182 and acct-999). Noticing increased errors for embeddings endpoints as well.
Maria: rollback completed, new pods are up and passing healthchecks. config-service logs show fewer `504` to billing.
Alex K: good. keep circuit breaker and token cache for now. we'll re-evaluate after stabilization.
Samir: next actions: 1) monitor for 15m stability window, 2) if stable, gradually remove temporary circuit breaker and keep cache in config with tuned TTL, 3) follow-up RCA to examine why billing-client latency spiked (upstream).
Jordan: triage note: billing-service in us-east reported higher p95 at same time; filing ticket to them for correlation.
Lia: CS update posted to affected customers; offering log bundle and ETA.
OncallBot: Incident priority: P1 (elevated disruption), paging team: @Samir assigned.
Samir: taking incident lead. handing monitoring and initial mitigations. will hand off to Maria in 45m for deep dive.
Maria: acknowledged, standing by for handoff at 18:40 UTC.
Alex K: small config to remove aggressive org-lookup for non-critical endpoints added. patch: ```routes: - path: /v1/embeddings - org_lookup: false``` deployed to canary.
Jordan: additional observation: high retry storms from SDK clients after initial timeout. we should consider rate-limiting retries client-side or adjust retry-after headers.
Samir: created temporary rate-limit rule to reduce burst retries from non-authenticated SDK traffic. rule id rl-temp-2177.
OpsBot: rule rl-temp-2177 applied at 18:10 UTC (limit: 50r/s per-ip burst 200).
Lia: support notes updated with mitigations and workaround steps for affected customers (recommend retry with exponential backoff).
Alex K: will schedule postmortem. please collect traces for 17:30-18:20 UTC and attach to the RCA.
Maria: copying runbook entries changed: org-lookup caching is now instrumented; adding a guard in the config push pipeline to prevent TTLs < 30s for org lookup.
Samir: monitoring window passed 16m with 5xx ~<3% and p95 latency improving. retaining temporary mitigations for 1h then incrementally revert.
Jordan: billing team acknowledged they had a degraded instance due to a library bug causing thread pool exhaustion - they're rolling a fix.
Lia: customer comms: posted update, offering detailed incident timeline and mitigation steps; asked customers to contact support for logs.
OncallBot: Handoff: Samir -> Maria at 18:41 UTC. Samir set status to `incident:monitoring`, Maria set to `incident:investigating`.
Maria: taking over. I'll coordinate RCA and timeline, aim to publish summarized postmortem in 24h. tagging SRE and platform infra.
Samir: leaving notes: scaled config-service, rolled back TTL change, added auth token cache, applied billing-client circuit breaker, temp rate-limit for retries.
Alex K: thanks everyone. please add any leftover actions to the incident board.
Lia: closing customer-facing update thread, will ping if escalations.
OpsBot: Incident summary (auto): root cause likely a cascade: billing-service degraded -> billing-client timeouts -> config-service backlog -> org-lookup TTL change amplified load -> auth retries -> control-plane 5xx surge. mitigations applied: scale, rollback, cache, circuit-breaker, temp rate-limit.
Maria: recorded for RCA. scheduling postmortem meeting.
Samir: marking handoff complete.
OncallBot: Incident thread archived at 18:52 UTC (monitoring).
